title: Central Nervous System — Brain and Spinal Cord

brain_development.secondary_vesicles: telencephalon → cerebrum. diencephalon → thalamus/hypothalamus. mesencephalon → midbrain. metencephalon → pons + cerebellum. myelencephalon → medulla oblongata.

cerebrum.surface: cerebral cortex = thin outer layer of GRAY MATTER. folds: gyri (ridges), sulci (shallow grooves), fissures (deep grooves). folding increases surface area.
cerebrum.white_matter: deep to cortex. myelinated axon tracts: commissural (corpus callosum — connects hemispheres), association (within same hemisphere), projection (cortex ↔ lower brain/spinal cord).
cerebrum.hemispheres: left + right, connected by CORPUS CALLOSUM. contralateral control: left hemisphere controls right body, vice versa.

frontal.location: anterior, separated from parietal by CENTRAL SULCUS
frontal.functions: voluntary motor (precentral gyrus = PRIMARY MOTOR CORTEX), planning, personality, judgement, executive function, speech production (BROCA'S AREA — usually left hemisphere)
frontal.precentral_gyrus: primary motor cortex. motor homunculus. controls voluntary movement. large areas for hands, face (fine motor).

parietal.functions: general somatic sensation (postcentral gyrus = PRIMARY SOMATOSENSORY CORTEX), spatial awareness, body position
parietal.postcentral_gyrus: primary somatosensory cortex. sensory homunculus. receives touch, pressure, pain, temperature from body.

temporal.functions: hearing (PRIMARY AUDITORY CORTEX), memory, olfaction, language comprehension (WERNICKE'S AREA — usually left hemisphere)

occipital.functions: vision (PRIMARY VISUAL CORTEX). processes visual input from retina.

lobes.insula: deep to lateral sulcus. 'island.' taste, visceral sensation, emotional awareness. sometimes called 5th lobe.

lateralization.left_hemisphere: language (Broca's + Wernicke's), math, logic, analytical processing in MOST people
lateralization.right_hemisphere: spatial awareness, face recognition, music, emotional interpretation, holistic processing
lateralization.note: both hemispheres do BOTH types — lateralization is about DOMINANCE, not exclusivity.

language_areas.brocas_area: frontal lobe (left). MOTOR speech. produces speech. damage → BROCA'S APHASIA: understands language but CAN'T SPEAK fluently (nonfluent/expressive aphasia).
language_areas.wernickes_area: temporal lobe (left). SENSORY speech. comprehends language. damage → WERNICKE'S APHASIA: speaks fluently but DOESN'T MAKE SENSE (fluent/receptive aphasia).
language_areas.arcuate_fasciculus: fiber bundle connecting Broca's and Wernicke's. damage → CONDUCTION APHASIA: can understand and speak but can't repeat what they hear.

basal_nuclei_ganglia.what: deep gray matter masses within cerebral white matter. caudate nucleus, putamen, globus pallidus. (putamen + globus pallidus = lentiform nucleus. caudate + putamen = striatum.)
basal_nuclei_ganglia.function: regulate voluntary motor activity. filter + inhibit unwanted movements. smooth out intended movements.
basal_nuclei_ganglia.disorders: Parkinson's (loss of dopamine input → rigidity, tremor). Huntington's (degeneration of caudate + putamen → involuntary movements, chorea).

thalamus.what: paired egg-shaped masses. ~80% of diencephalon. GATEWAY TO CEREBRAL CORTEX.
thalamus.function: relay station for ALL sensory input EXCEPT OLFACTION (smell goes directly to cortex). sorts, edits, filters sensory info before sending to cortex. also roles in motor, emotion, memory.

hypothalamus.what: below thalamus. small but critical. forms floor of 3rd ventricle.
functions: AUTONOMIC control center — regulates ANS (heart rate, BP, GI motility, pupil size)
ENDOCRINE control — controls pituitary gland (anterior via releasing/inhibiting hormones, posterior stores oxytocin + ADH)
EMOTIONAL responses (rage, fear, pleasure — with limbic system)

diencephalon.epithalamus: pineal gland → melatonin (sleep cycle). also contains choroid plexus (produces CSF in 3rd ventricle).

brainstem.note: connects cerebrum to spinal cord. all ascending/descending tracts pass through here. three regions top to bottom:

midbrain.cerebral_peduncles: anterior. large fiber tracts carrying motor signals from cortex DOWN to spinal cord.
midbrain.superior_colliculi: visual reflexes (head/eye tracking of moving objects).
midbrain.inferior_colliculi: auditory reflexes (startle reflex to loud sounds, head turning toward sound).
midbrain.substantia_nigra: dopamine-producing neurons. projects to basal nuclei. degeneration → Parkinson's.

pons.what: bridge between cerebellum and brainstem. anterior bulge.
pons.functions: relay between cerebrum and cerebellum. contains nuclei for cranial nerves V, VI, VII. PNEUMOTAXIC + APNEUSTIC centers modify breathing rhythm (work with medulla's respiratory centers).

medulla_oblongata.what: most inferior brainstem region. continuous with spinal cord at foramen magnum.
vital_centers: CARDIOVASCULAR center — regulates heart rate + blood vessel diameter (blood pressure)
RESPIRATORY center — sets basic breathing rhythm (ventral respiratory group = forced breathing, dorsal respiratory group = quiet breathing)
other reflexes: VOMITING, SWALLOWING, COUGHING, SNEEZING, HICCUPPING
medulla_oblongata.pyramids: anterior bulges. PYRAMIDAL (corticospinal) tracts cross here — DECUSSATION OF PYRAMIDS. that's why left brain controls right body.
medulla_oblongata.cranial_nerves: nuclei for CN VIII, IX, X, XI, XII

cerebellum.location: posterior to pons + medulla. inferior to occipital lobes. connected via 3 cerebellar peduncles.
cerebellum.structure: two hemispheres + vermis (midline). surface = folia (leaf-like folds). cortex = gray matter. interior = white matter (arbor vitae = tree of life pattern).
function: coordinates voluntary movements — does NOT initiate movement. REFINES + SMOOTHS.
motor learning (procedural memory — riding a bike, typing)
cerebellum.damage: ataxia (loss of coordination, staggering gait, overshooting movements), intention tremor, loss of balance, slurred speech (dysarthria). affects SAME SIDE (ipsilateral — does NOT cross).

meninges.note: three CT membranes covering brain + spinal cord. protection.

dura_mater.what: TOUGH outer layer. 'tough mother.' two layers around brain: periosteal (fused to skull) + meningeal. ONE layer around spinal cord (epidural space between dura and vertebral bone).
dura_mater.dural_folds: falx cerebri (between cerebral hemispheres), falx cerebelli (between cerebellar hemispheres), tentorium cerebelli (between cerebrum and cerebellum).
dura_mater.dural_sinuses: venous channels between dural layers. drain blood from brain.

meninges.arachnoid_mater: middle layer. web-like. SUBARACHNOID SPACE between arachnoid and pia contains CSF + blood vessels.
meninges.pia_mater: DELICATE inner layer. clings directly to brain/spinal cord surface. highly vascular. follows every fold.

cerebrospinal_fluid.produced_by: CHOROID PLEXUS — specialized ependymal cells in ventricle walls. ~500 mL/day. ~150 mL circulating at any time (replaced ~3x/day).
cerebrospinal_fluid.path: lateral ventricles → interventricular foramen (of Monro) → 3rd ventricle → cerebral aqueduct (of Sylvius) → 4th ventricle → into subarachnoid space (via lateral apertures of Luschka + median aperture of Magendie).
cerebrospinal_fluid.reabsorbed_by: arachnoid villi (granulations) projecting into dural sinuses → returned to venous blood.
cerebrospinal_fluid.functions: cushions brain (buoyancy — brain weighs ~1500g but only ~50g in CSF). delivers nutrients. removes waste. chemical stability.
cerebrospinal_fluid.lumbar_puncture: spinal tap at L3-L5 (below conus medullaris at L1-L2). samples CSF for diagnosis (meningitis, hemorrhage).

spinal_cord.location: foramen magnum → conus medullaris (L1-L2). below that: cauda equina (horse's tail — bundle of spinal nerve roots).
spinal_cord.filum_terminale: thin thread of pia mater anchoring cord to coccyx.

structure.gray_matter: INSIDE. butterfly/H shape. dorsal horns (sensory interneurons), ventral horns (motor neurons → skeletal muscle), lateral horns (T1-L2 only — sympathetic neurons).
structure.white_matter: OUTSIDE (opposite of brain!). organized into columns/funiculi: dorsal, lateral, ventral. contain ascending (sensory) + descending (motor) tracts.
structure.central_canal: center. contains CSF. continuous with ventricles.

ascending_sensory.dorsal_columns: fine touch, vibration, proprioception. IPSILATERAL until medulla where they cross. fasciculus gracilis (lower body) + fasciculus cuneatus (upper body).
ascending_sensory.spinothalamic: pain, temperature, crude touch. cross at SPINAL CORD level. lateral spinothalamic = pain+temp. anterior spinothalamic = crude touch.
ascending_sensory.spinocerebellar: proprioception TO cerebellum. ipsilateral. unconscious proprioception.

descending_motor.corticospinal_lateral: voluntary movement. crosses at PYRAMIDAL DECUSSATION in medulla. fine, skilled movements.
descending_motor.corticospinal_anterior: voluntary movement. stays ipsilateral until spinal level, then crosses. trunk/proximal muscles.
descending_motor.rubrospinal: from red nucleus. flexor muscle tone.

components: 2. SENSORY (afferent) NEURON — transmits signal to CNS
3. INTEGRATION CENTER — CNS processing (may be just one synapse or multiple interneurons)
4. MOTOR (efferent) NEURON — transmits signal to effector
5. EFFECTOR — muscle or gland that carries out response
reflex_arc.stretch_reflex: MONOSYNAPTIC. simplest. sensory → motor. ONE synapse. EX: patellar (knee-jerk) reflex. muscle spindle detects stretch → sensory neuron → spinal cord → motor neuron → same muscle contracts. NO interneuron.
reflex_arc.withdrawal_flexor_reflex: POLYSYNAPTIC. pain → flexor contraction + extensor relaxation on same side (withdrawal). crossed extensor reflex on opposite side (support).

blood_brain_barrier.what: tight junctions between capillary endothelial cells in brain. astrocyte foot processes reinforce. selectively permeable.
blood_brain_barrier.passes: O2, CO2, glucose, amino acids, fat-soluble molecules (including alcohol, anesthetics, many drugs).
blood_brain_barrier.blocked: most large molecules, most hydrophilic drugs, proteins, toxins, pathogens (usually).
blood_brain_barrier.absent_at: hypothalamus (needs to monitor blood chemistry), vomiting center (needs to detect toxins).

CVA_stroke.ischemic: blood clot blocks cerebral artery. ~85% of strokes. tissue dies from O2 deprivation.
CVA_stroke.hemorrhagic: blood vessel ruptures. blood compresses tissue. ~15% of strokes.
CVA_stroke.effects: depend on location. motor cortex damage = paralysis. Broca's = can't speak. right hemisphere = spatial neglect.

clinical.traumatic_brain_injury: concussion (mild), contusion (bruising), epidural hematoma (arterial — rapid, lens-shaped on CT, middle meningeal artery), subdural hematoma (venous — slower, crescent on CT, bridging veins).
clinical.meningitis: inflammation of meninges. bacterial (emergency) or viral (usually less severe). stiff neck, fever, headache. diagnosed via lumbar puncture.
clinical.hydrocephalus: excess CSF accumulation. blocked drainage or overproduction. increases intracranial pressure. in infants: head enlarges (fontanelles open). treatment: shunt.
